description: PP-OCRv4 mobile text detector. Not here to read text: here to answer 'is this a screenshot, a document, or a photo of a whiteboard'. Build plan §4.2 auto-excludes those from memories, and they are a large fraction of a real phone library.

normalisation.calibration_note: The output map is ALREADY a probability: PP-OCRv4's DBHead applies F.sigmoid inside forward and returns the sigmoided shrink_maps at inference. Applying sigmoid a second time -- which this config did -- maps [0,1] onto [0.5, 0.731], so with det_db_thresh 0.3 every pixel of every image exceeds the threshold, every photo reads as 100% text, and the entire library is excluded as screenshots. Found by Codex; confirmed against ppocr/modeling/heads/det_db_head.py. 0.3 is PaddleOCR's own det_db_thresh default.

license.training_data: PaddleOCR's own Chinese and English corpora. Baidu publishes the detection weights under the repository licence rather than a separate model licence, which is the cleaner of the two arrangements this registry deals with.
license.note: Desk assessment only. Apache-2.0 on both code and weights, which is why this is the detector of choice over better-scoring alternatives with murkier checkpoints.

notes:
PLACEHOLDER FOR THE SHAPE until the ONNX export is produced and pinned. The source_url names the PaddleOCR repository, not a specific ONNX artifact, while this config asserts tensor names, fp16 and output shapes -- and the runtime binds by exact tensor name. Codex was right that an unpinned export has no business in a 'runnable' pipeline, and this file had three separate errors before that point, so it stays out until someone exports and verifies it.

THE ERRORS, RECORDED SO THEY ARE NOT REINTRODUCED:
  * DOUBLE SIGMOID (release-blocking). The DB head already sigmoids; applying it again squashes probabilities into [0.5,0.731] and, at threshold 0.3, classifies every photo as entirely text. The whole library would have been excluded as screenshots, silently.
  * RGB instead of BGR. PP-OCRv4 detection trains and infers on cv2.imread output, which is BGR, with no conversion anywhere in the inference path.
  * A 640x640 letterbox. That is the TRAINING crop. Inference preserves aspect with the longer side limited to 960 and both dimensions rounded to a multiple of 32. Letterboxing would also have diluted the coverage fraction with padding, since padding contains no text -- so the measure this model exists to produce would have been wrong even after the other two were fixed.

DETECTION ONLY, NO RECOGNITION. The product question is 'should this image be excluded from a memory', and text COVERAGE answers it. Running the recogniser would transcribe the words -- bank balances, medical results, private messages -- which is the content people would least want stored, and it buys nothing the coverage fraction does not already give. A privacy decision, not a cost one; do not reverse it without a specific reason and a consent scope.

THRESHOLDING IS THE CALLER'S JOB. 'Text-dense' does not mean 'not a memory': a whiteboard covered in writing at a family event is both. Face presence and EXIF (a screenshot has no lens data) are what separate them, so that boundary lives in the ranking engine where it can be tuned and explained.
